sections.title: Playing Together
sections.content_summary: Bela introduces her family — brothers Banku Bhaiya and little Bishu — and describes playing chhupan-chhupai (hide and seek) and peek-a-boo together outside. The family has planted a flowering garden where relatives, friends, and neighbours gather to sit, talk, share jokes, and relax in the evenings. The section establishes the home and its open spaces as a site of joyful togetherness across generations.

sections.title: Singing Together
sections.content_summary: On rainy days, the family sits under a garden shelter and plays games like antakshari and snakes and ladders. Dadiji (grandmother) and mother make hot pakodas and tea for everyone, including the grandparents. Dadiji sings folk songs about the rain, which she has taught the children — an example of intergenerational transmission of traditional songs. A rain-inspired folk poem is presented in the section.

sections.title: Laughing Together
sections.content_summary: Dadaji (grandfather) teaches the children traditional games he played as a boy, and joins in their games himself. The pet dog Shiru is described as a full member of the family — played with, fed, and never hurt. The section introduces the idea that families come in many sizes and forms, and that a family can include animals. Neighbourhood families are mentioned as part of the broader community around the child.

sections.title: Helping Each Other
sections.content_summary: Family members share daily household work: Dadiji oils and braids Bela's hair while humming songs; parents cook, clean, and shop together; Banku Bhaiya helps chop vegetables; Bela helps Dadaji in the garden. The section also introduces their close neighbour Munni and her mother Kusum Mausi, who participates in festivals and makes rangoli from colours derived from dried flowers — a traditional Indian craft practice. Children are shown as active contributors to family routines from an early age.

sections.title: Fun with Family and Friends
sections.content_summary: On a holiday, the family goes to the park with Dadaji and joins friends playing pitthoo — a traditional Indian street game involving stacked stones and a ball. Two teams form, with Dadaji actively participating. After the game, Dadaji buys everyone ice cream. The section shows how outdoor play with family and friends, including intergenerational participation, creates joyful shared memories.

sections.title: Let us reflect
sections.content_summary: A structured reflection section with four sub-tasks: writing about how family shows love and the games students play with friends; drawing happy moments with family; discussing what is learnt from elders and how community care extends beyond family; and a word-search activity to find games-related words. These tasks consolidate the chapter's themes of family bonds, play, and community care.

dual_strand.human_cultural: Family bonds, intergenerational transmission of traditional games and folk songs, mutual aid in daily chores, and traditional art practices such as rangoli using dried flowers
